newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Party officials shot at as Albania heads for poll.
newsitem.headline: Party officials shot at as Albania heads for poll.

text.p: Albania's Socialist party said two of its officials were shot at on Monday on their way to an election rally, in the latest sign of tension in the run-up to snap elections on June 29.
Both Albania's main parties have recently started to take their campaign into hostile areas ahead of the election, intended to end months of chaos and civil disorder.
The Socialist Party said in a statement that an armed gang fired on two of its officials as they headed for a rally in the north, forcing them to turn back but leaving them unhurt.

The party, a traditional opponent of President Sali Berisha's Democrats but currently in the multi-party government of national unity, said at least five bullets hit the body of the car and penetrated the seats.
The car was carrying party secretary general Rexhep Mejdani and a member of its national steering committee, Bektash Zeneli, to a rally in the town of Puke.
A party spokesman told Reuters the officials' police escort had been waylaid by unidentified people. No independent witnesses were immediately available.

After weeks of rioting and unrest following the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes earlier this year, Albania is still in a state of emergency with parts of the country out of government control.

In the southern town of Vlore, residents said there was shooting in the air for about an hour in the morning in different parts of town, following rumours that Berisha, who is from the north, might visit.
They said the shots caused panic but no major injuries.
